subject: Information Theory
title: Letters Aren't Equal
description: A quick, practical guide to Letters Aren't Equal.

hook.text: The letter E appears 13% of the time in English. Z appears 0.07%. They carry very different amounts of information.

buildup.text: Shannon computed: rare letters carry more information because they're more surprising when they appear.

discovery.text: E carries about 3 bits of information. Z carries over 10 bits. Rarity equals surprise equals information.

twist.text: This is why crossword puzzles reward rare letters more. Q and Z score higher because they're harder to place.

climax.text: Shannon showed English has about 1.0 to 1.5 bits of entropy per letter—far less than its 4.7-bit maximum.

punchline.text: Common letters say little. Rare letters say a lot.

quiz.question: Why does the letter Z carry more information than E?
options: It's at the end of the alphabet
It's much rarer and therefore more surprising
It's used in more important words
